chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hilāl, from ʿUqbah ibn Khālid, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who said, “This ship belongs to so-and-so,” and he did not specify what was in it, while there was food in it. Is the man to be given the ship and what is in it?
He عليه السلام said: “It belongs to the one for whom it was bequeathed, unless its owner excluded what was in it. The heirs have no share in it.”

key_terms.السَّفِينَةُ: the ship that is the subject of the bequest

ai.seo_question: If someone bequeaths a ship without mentioning its contents, do the contents also belong to the beneficiary?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a bequest of a ship when the contents were not separately mentioned. The ruling is that the ship and its contents go to the beneficiary of the bequest unless the owner explicitly excluded the contents, and in that case the heirs do not have a claim over what was included in the bequest.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5510 - Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn narrated from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hilal from Uqbah ibn Khalid from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man who said:
"This ship belongs to so-and-so," without specifying what was inside it, and there was food in it. Should the man be given the ship and what is inside it?
Imam (as) said: "It belongs to the one to whom it was bequeathed, unless its owner explicitly excluded what was inside it. The heirs have no claim over it."
